summary: Peer objection-handling training between two closers, arranged in the 07/03 team meeting. Opens with fifteen minutes of personal catch-up — Richard is in Bansko, Bulgaria, Michael is in Medellin moving to Brazil — then they run mock calls with Richard playing a 28-year-old prospect who wants to lose 25 lb after a breakup, and Michael running the price objection and the spouse objection. Richard, the newer closer on this offer, coaches Michael, the more experienced one, throughout. They agree to run daily roleplay after the sales meeting from Wednesday onward and book Monday separately.
notable: Michael improvised and pitched a named one-month tier — 'we have a program called Love It or Leave It, where you can come in for a month and it's $1,200' with full client access — and Richard critiqued the technique without ever questioning the price or whether the tier exists.

Richard's coached spouse-objection play has the prospect proceeding against a partner's refusal: 'let's not even put the responsibility on her for making decision. Let's just do it' and 'Buy a bouquet of flowers, otherwise I'll pay for it. Say sorry to her.'

The same play uses predicted marital breakdown as leverage — 'just show them exactly what will happen in 12 months. If he just sits around, becomes fat and his wife's probably going to want to leave him because he isn't being better.'
Richard's stated doctrine: 'there's two objections, money and fear. The rest, all is [nonsense]', and on partner objections 'a lot of times it's just a smoke screen, like 99% of the time'.

Explicit coaching to substitute 'nervousness' for 'fear' because prospects will admit to the softer word — 'it's the exact same. It's just a different word for it. And that makes people admit it. Easier.'
Both closers describe leaving previous offers where nothing was moving; Richard says he still has three calls left on his other offer next week, so he was running two offers concurrently.

Michael on why he nearly did not take the job: 'I was at Andrew's calendar when I first came on. I was like, dude, this guy's taking nine calls a day. He's only making six grand this month or something.'

Richard, describing the previous day's call — the Anthony Boon call in this same batch: 'yesterday I had someone who was 100% able to [buy]... He wasn't going to [pay], but he was thanking me for actually helping him, holding up the mirror. He didn't even have rent money.'
Michael discloses his own shoulder injury and 10-15 lb gain and plans to join the programme as a client; Richard tells him to message Trevor for exercise substitutions.
Richard names his external sales coach, Samuel Hine, as the source of the objection-handling framework he is teaching, and offers to send Michael the training materials over Slack.
Richard says every Fathom recording is automatically pushed into the SalesKake records.
